text:
monitoring-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: control-plane heartbeat missing for region asia-southeast2 (ase2). Last seen: 1958004305. All control-plane API endpoints returning 502/timeout.

alice_oncall: ack — I'm oncall. Paging @ben_sre and @carla_infra. Starting quick triage. Can others hold on standby? :eyes:

ben_sre: on it. grabbing k8s control-plane pod state now.

ben_sre: quick dump:
```
kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l app=control-plane -o wide
NAME                          READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
control-plane-0               0/3     CrashLoopBackOff   12         3h
control-plane-1               1/3     Running            2          3h
```

ben_sre: logs show API server failing on leader-election timeouts and etcd connection refused.

carla_infra: I see provider console shows an internal network maintenance event in ase2 starting ~1958004200. They list "virtual network reconfiguration" for some subnets. Link: https://provider.status/ase2/maintenance (monitoring notifies more details).

dan_runtime: model-serving nodes (worker GPUs) are still up and serving locally, but the control-plane outage prevents autoscaler and routing updates. Some requests are queued at prod-router.

eric_neteng: running traceroute to control-plane VIP shows hop drop at LB:
```
traceroute 10.34.12.5
 1  prod-router 0.8 ms
 2  provider-lb 100.2 ms *
 3  * * *
```

eric_neteng: provider's LB returns 503 for health checks to controller backends. Looks like backend pool removed or health check failing.

fiona_prodops: customer impact check: the hosted API for ase2 is degraded; new sessions fail to initialize (function call failures). Existing long-running streams mostly continue for a bit. Early estimate: ~12% of traffic hit ase2.

alice_oncall: decision time: failover traffic to ap-southeast1 (ap-south-east-1). Is capacity available to absorb 100%?

ben_sre: Dedicated fallback pools have spare capacity for ~2x typical burst, but we'll need to spin up a couple node groups to be safe. Scaling steps:
1) trigger reserved-node warmup for dedicated-fallback cluster
2) update routing policy to shift 70% now and 100% if metrics look ok

carla_infra: provider maintenance ticket shows "config rollback" is possible but ETA uncertain. Recommend we failover rather than wait.

dan_runtime: note: when we shift, KV cache hits will drop and token cost will spike temporarily. We should enable aggressive cache-warmup on fallback.

alice_oncall: ben, carla — can you execute failover plan? I'll coordinate communications and open SEV2. Fiona, can you prepare a customer status update?

ben_sre: executing step 1 now.
```
infra-cli clusters scale --cluster dedicated-fallback --nodes +8 --reason "ase2 control-plane outage"
```

ben_sre: nodes requested, provider reports instances launching. ETA ~3m.

carla_infra: updating routing policy to split traffic. Using deploy-bot to update traffic weights.
```
deploy-bot update-route --region-weight ase2=30,ap-se1=70 --apply --note "auto-failover ase2"
```

deploy-bot: applied new weights. Rolling config pushed to edge-router pool.

alice_oncall: starting to shift 70% now. Monitoring latency, error-rate, and token cost.

fiona_prodops: posting incident page: https://status.redwood/incident/1958004321 — initial note posted, will update in 15m.

eric_neteng: LB health checks in provider console now show backend pool restored for ap-se1; ase2 still failing health checks.

ben_sre: dedicated-fallback nodes are healthy. Autoscaler still blocked from ase2 due to missing control-plane signals, but fallback cluster up.

dan_runtime: traffic now flowing to ap-se1. Observability: request latency +90ms and token cost +6% so far. No spike in error-rate after shift.

alice_oncall: good. keep shift at 70% for 10m, then decide. Also open upstream provider support ticket with priority.

carla_infra: provider SR opened: SR-987654 — they acknowledge maintenance and are investigating backend pool config.

ben_sre: summary of next actions:
- keep 70% split, monitor for 15m
- if stable, move to 100% and mark ase2 as drained for new sessions
- collect etcd + apiserver logs from control-plane nodes for postmortem
- prepare rollback plan if provider restores network quickly (we'll need to re-sync leader-election)

fiona_prodops: customer comms draft ready, posting now. Notifying enterprise customers with ase2 commitments.

alice_oncall: declaring SEV2. Incident lead: alice_oncall. Scribe: ben_sre. Next update in 10m or on major change. :white_check_mark:

monitoring-bot: Alert suppressed for region ase2 after routing policy change. Continued monitoring enabled.

ben_sre: capturing logs for timeline:
```
kubectl -n kube-system logs control-plane-0 --tail=200 > /tmp/ase2-controlplane-logs-1958004321.log
```

carla_infra: provider says config change was accidental and they're rolling back; ETA unknown. We'll keep shift until they confirm stability.

alice_oncall: thanks team. Keep chat for updates. If error-rate crosses threshold, we'll escalate to SEV1 and invoke global failover procedures.

fiona_prodops: incident page updated with mitigation steps and next ETA.

ben_sre: noted — collecting artifacts for postmortem.

alice_oncall: end of initial triage.
